properties.description:
# Nested task execution and review

Required MVP work. The MVP cannot be complete until this package and its required reviews are accepted. Follow the updated MVP delivery plan and execute each implementation stage serially, waiting for its human review before the next.

1. Model ownership: task containment, execution, review, check attempts and derived state have one owning model. Typed mutators atomically preserve invariants for UI, MCP and agents. No UI-only repairs, weak typing, authored JavaScript, ignored diagnostics or duplicated policy.
2. Dependency truth: every rendered dependency traces to an actual relation. Containment and review coverage must not invent prerequisite edges. Reject dependency/containment cycles and redundant direct edges with indirect witness paths. Never hide invalid edges as if fixed; diagnostics use the theme error token.
3. Readiness: Queued means executable now but not started. Waiting has a concrete model reason: incomplete prerequisite, pending acceptance or required human review. Queuing a parent admits unfinished descendants atomically; it never starts execution or revives completed/abandoned work. All placements remain applicable to all tasks; the Activity board remains top-level only.
4. Parent state proposal: execution placement is computed from children and required gates, not independently editable into contradiction. Parent actions operate on descendants. The model proposal must present a complete state table for backlog, queued, running, waiting, mixed terminal, failed checks and abandonment before wiring consumers. Work performed and work accepted are distinct facts.
5. Acceptance: unresolved required review/check gates prevent completion of the work they cover, including prerequisite branches in that acceptance scope. Previously accepted review boundaries stay accepted. Reviewers can finish a review without accepting every task. A review may reject work without becoming a dependency deadlock. No fabricated historical completion or approval.
6. Iteration: author correction and resubmission stay in the same task scope. Do not require a new outer task or require feedback categorization against original tasks. Preserve submitted versions, actor/outcome/evidence and attempt history without drawing duplicate instances of the same task. Separate new work is created only for explicitly deferred scope. No mandatory round label.
7. Recursive representation: execution, review and correction steps use nested tasks and the same node representation at every depth. Implement itself can have children. Expand/collapse is independent per node and retains the parent title/type, computed state, avatar, direct-child count and controls.
8. Node information: state circle, chat actor avatar, type and optional title, bare direct-child count immediately before chevron. Tooltip identifies direct-child count. Type and title are separate. Review/Correct may omit a title; implementation work must remain identifiable. Collapsing retains the assignee. Review circles display outcome. Breadcrumbs own parent context; no repeated parent or blocking text.
9. Geometry: rows follow dependencies, placing prerequisites as close below successors as occupied space allows. Distinct dependent tasks cannot share a row. Fork and merge anchors align with the left main chain; sibling branches get neighbouring columns; a post-merge chain may reuse a column. Orthogonal segments with rounded quarter-circle corners leave predecessor circle top and enter successor circle bottom continuously across nesting. The first task column is the leftmost permitted routing path. Never attach to frame borders, cross labels, or share a trunk that falsely implies an unrelated task connection.
10. Focus: double-click focuses a task; expand stays in the current scope. Preserve immediate external prerequisites AND successors for every boundary-crossing connection, including multiple entries, exits and mixed internal attachment points. Deduplicate by task identity while retaining all real edges. Stop external expansion after one hop; further links are navigable with counts/tooltips. Navigation/back restores focus, expansion, zoom and scroll.
11. Now: each unfinished expanded scope has its own state separator. It does not imply a common timestamp scale. The readiness model must distinguish not-yet-started waiting from executed work awaiting acceptance so dependencies are not reversed to satisfy a cosmetic separator. Completed-only subgraphs do not need a divider. No visible Planned/State history header; explain by tooltip.
12. Checks: display actual check runs, results and attempts from the check owner with Broccoli as executor. Tie results to exact inputs/submitted revision; stale, failed, cancelled and interrupted runs never satisfy a gate. No synthetic success or copied check state. Expose the existing TypeScript checks for TheBroccoli, BtrTemplate and PersoTemplate.
13. Same data everywhere: graph, editor, Activity board, review and owner API agree on placements, outcomes and relations after reload. Review UI preserves independent reviewer decisions and task states. Keep the underlying model inspectable.
14. Serial delivery and review: execute one implementation stage at a time. Each stage has a required human review; the following stage depends on that review passing. Use the review surface to inspect the plan and task criteria; feedback may be given in chat or attached to a task. A failed or incomplete check or rejected review never authorizes the next stage. Do not infer safe parallelism from different filenames or passing checks. Parallel execution remains out of scope until deterministic dependency/impact and conflicting-write analysis, isolation and integration rules are available and explicitly approved.
15. Delivery: replace superseded range/history/loop machinery completely within the replaced scope; no compatibility layer or duplicate authority. Keep declared dependencies direct and correctly layered. Verify narrow/wide layouts, keyboard operation, progressive feedback and representative deep/branching graphs. At the development checkpoint run required repository gates and inspect rendered UI; tests alone are not visual acceptance.

Deferred
Duration/time-axis visualization, scheduling triggers, UID redesign (separate backlog task), and multi-agent orchestration. Generated images are exploratory references; their missing edges, centered branch origins and single-entry/exit examples are explicitly not accepted requirements.

Review decisions still needed
Exact parent placement aggregation and abandonment semantics; durable review attempt representation inside the reused task; terminology replacing the old review-only task where appropriate. The view is named Task graph. These are visible plan decisions, not silently inferred implementation approvals.
